messages.author: 16bac0a0bbd38012
messages.subject: Predicting species occupancy over time
parts:
I would like to use brms for predicting species occupancy over time in a Bernoulli logistic regression and wondered if there is a way to make it a dynamic model, with presence at the first time step t informing the probability of presence at time t+1, t+2, etc.? 

Also, if I have coordinates for each data point, is there a way to make the model spatially explicit?  

Thank you!!

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Predicting species occupancy over time
parts:
brms supports a few autocorrelation structures (for instance ARMA structures), but they are not supported in a bernoulli model.

You could try fitting splines for the time and spatial correlations. For instance,

y ~ ... + s(time, by = species) + t2(x, z, by = species)

where x and z are the sptial coordinates. The by = species terms implies fitting separate splines for each species.

Thank you!

I would like to implement this model using brms but am unsure of how to translate it from Jags to brms. This is the Jags version:

model{
  beta[1] ~ dnorm(0,3.68)
  beta[2] ~ dnorm(0,3.68)
  beta[3] ~ dnorm(0,3.68)
  sigma ~ dunif(0,1)
  for(i in 1 : length(n)){
    for(j in 1 : length(year)){
      
      y[i,j] ~ dbern(p[i,j])
      p[i,j] ~ dnorm(ilogit(beta[1] + beta[2] * x1[i,j] + beta[3] * x2[i,j]), sigma^2)
      
    }
    
}}

Would it be something like this:

prior <- c(set_prior("normal(0,0.368)", class = "b", coef = "x1"), set_prior("normal(0,0.368)", class = "b", coef = "x2"), set_prior("uniform(0,1)", class = "sigma"))

?
How should i deal with the subscripts i and j? Is class="sigma" correct for the prior on sigma^2?
